meta_description: Got a Calgary speeding ticket? Check Alberta demerit bands, the court threshold, official response options, and what to review before acting.
h1: Calgary Speeding Tickets: Demerits and What to Do Next
hook: Calgary officer-issued speeding tickets use Alberta's provincial demerit schedule, ranging from two to six points depending on the alleged speed.
bullets: The Alberta speeding schedule applies to officer-issued Calgary tickets.
The schedule rises from two points up to 15 km/h over to six points at 51 km/h or more over.
Speeding at 51 km/h or more over the limit requires a court appearance.
Use the instructions and response deadline printed on the ticket.
what:
What a Calgary speeding ticket can mean

For an officer-issued ticket, Alberta's current schedule assigns two demerit points up to 15 km/h over, three for 16 to 30 km/h over, four for 31 to 50 km/h over, and six for 51 km/h or more over. The highest band also requires a court appearance.

Demerit points are applied on the conviction date and remain on the driving record for two years. The existing record matters because Alberta's suspension thresholds differ for fully licensed and GDL drivers.

For the complete provincial process, read how to fight a speeding ticket in Alberta, including online response options, the document checklist and when to get agent help.
how:
Is it worth getting help with a Calgary speeding ticket?

Start with the alleged offence, your response deadline and the evidence. You can use the official online response options yourself. If you want help managing an eligible pre-trial matter, compare the quoted cost, what work is included and whether trial representation is separate. Do not assume a paid service will obtain a withdrawal or reduction.

Online ticket-agent help for Calgary drivers

Fabsy provides online ticket administration and permitted agent representation for eligible Calgary traffic matters. Secure intake, authorization, disclosure tracking and file updates are handled online. Fabsy reviews the disclosure, prepares a fact-specific prosecutor-review submission and explains any Crown response for your instructions. Fabsy is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice.

Read Rapid Resolution service details and compare ticket-service scope and fees. Trial representation and government fines are separate.

How to review the ticket

Check whether the ticket was issued by an officer or generated through automated enforcement, because the record consequences and evidence can differ. Confirm the alleged offence, location, response deadline, and instructions printed on the ticket.

Preserve any relevant photographs, dashcam video, or documents. Request the available disclosure and review the officer notes, measurement-device records, location, signs, and conditions before choosing a response through Alberta's current ticket process.

Where to find Calgary traffic court information

The Calgary Courts Centre is at 601 5th Street SW. The official court directory lists Calgary Traffic in Suite 203-S and lists Calgary Regional separately. Use the court named on your ticket: a nearby community is not necessarily handled by the same office.

Check the Calgary Court of Justice location page for current location and contact information. Follow the appearance or response instructions on your own ticket.

Can I respond online without hiring an agent?

Alberta's Traffic Tickets Digital Service offers online ticket-response options, including payment, time-to-pay requests and disputes. The Court of Justice says this service does not handle municipal bylaw tickets. Read the official response instructions and your notice before choosing an option.

For a step-by-step overview, read how to fight a traffic ticket in Alberta. Compare the province-wide speeding guide and Alberta demerit-point guide. If yours is a camera notice, start with the photo-radar guide.

How Rapid Resolution works

  1. Secure intake and authorization. Upload the ticket and complete the digital consent and authorization so Fabsy can check eligibility and the printed deadline.
  2. Disclosure request and tracking. Fabsy requests the available disclosure and tracks it to the file.
  3. Disclosure analysis and prosecutor review. Fabsy uses technology-assisted analysis with qualified review to prepare a fact-specific request. Complete, readable disclosure is reviewed and the next authorized prosecutor step is prepared or submitted within 48 hours after it is received and matched to your file.
  4. Immediate client updates. Fabsy notifies the client when the file changes, explains any Crown response in plain language and follows the client's authorized direction.
next:
Start Rapid Resolution

Upload a readable copy of the ticket and complete the digital authorization before the deadline printed on the ticket. Rapid Resolution starts immediately and, once complete disclosure arrives, analyzes and advances your eligible Alberta ticket within 48 hours, pursuing a withdrawal or a reduced charge that may lower the fine and/or demerits.

Free Ticket Check; Rapid Resolution: Photo Radar costs $79 CAD plus 5% GST ($82.95 total) for eligible Alberta registered-owner automated enforcement notices, with no success fee. Rapid Resolution costs $198 CAD plus applicable GST for other eligible Alberta pre-trial matters. The Insurance Impact & Renewal Planning Report costs $49 CAD plus applicable GST, or Rapid Resolution and the report cost $229 CAD plus applicable GST. Trial representation is quoted separately; government fines and out-of-scope matters are separate.

The 48-hour clock begins only after complete, readable disclosure is received and matched to the file. It covers Fabsy's review and next authorized action, not Crown response time or the date of a final outcome.

Outcomes depend on the charge, evidence, procedure and prosecutor. A withdrawal, reduction, lower fine, fewer demerits or insurance result is not promised. If the Crown rejects Fabsy's efforts to reduce your original fine or demerits, or withdraw your ticket, and none of those improvements is obtained, Fabsy refunds your service fee within 30 days of receiving the rejection. Payment does not start the 30-day refund clock.
